newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar remains under $300 as trade sell.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar remains under $300 as trade sell.

text.p: White sugar futures drifted slightly lower in light activity as the spot March contract proved content to remain under the $300 barrier, traders said on Tuesday.
One leading trade house was reported to be a good outright seller of March with the nearby March/May spread active and again moving to a discount.
Traders said the weakness of the London market was a spill-over effect of the continued fund liquidation in New York, which was expected to fall further despite bargain-hunting at the lows.
At 1254 GMT March stood 60 cents down at an intraday low of $297.00 and May down 20 cents at $297.50. Volume stayed on the light side at 272 lots.

In its daily report, statistician F.O. Licht said Friday's CFTC report showed speculators and funds had a much higher net long position than anticipated, undermining sentiment as more liquidation seemed to be on the cards.
"This, together with bearish fundamentals and slack end-user demand is likely to keep prices under pressure," it said.
Traders said they would continue to watch the fortunes of the March/March premium, which nearly reached $70 during Monday's session as the New York market continued to fall.
The spot premium has been widely forecast to narrow, possibly to as low as $60.
Technical analysts said the short-term direction of the London market was likely to be down, pegging March support at $296.50 followed by $295.10, the low scored on December 10.
In physical news, Hong Kong traders said South Korea recently bought up to five cargoes of sugar from Thailand for delivery in March or April but details of the price were unclear.
Other market sources said Indonesia could have bought some 100,000 tonnes of white sugar over the past few days, most likely from Thailand.
Volume in Paris was heavier than in London at 494 lots, possibly on account of pre-hedging against the European Union's weekly Wednesday tender for export licences.
March was down 80 cents at $297.00 and May down by the same amount at $297.50.
